Class ReferenceRateCard

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.design.value.ratecard.ReferenceRateCard
All Implemented Interfaces:
RateCard
public final class ReferenceRateCard extends Object implements RateCard
A RateCard backed by a bundled, dated table of indicative reference figures — published cloud-provider egress rates, interconnect port fees, and on-prem/colocation midpoints — compiled so the value-realization models work out of the box without a live connection or caller-supplied rates.

Every value it returns is tagged PriceSource.REFERENCE and the card carries a disclaimer() making clear these are estimates, not quotes: cloud egress rates are standard-tier US/North-America headline prices, and Equinix-side figures are indicative fallbacks that should be superseded by the live Fabric Pricing API (use a LayeredRateCard with EquinixRateCard ahead of this one).

Because the bundled table is deliberately coarse, the lookups are coarse too: connection(...) matches on bandwidth alone — the smallest tabulated tier at or above the request, linearly extrapolated (with an EXTRAPOLATED note) above the top tier — and ignores connection type, metro, and term; cloudRouter(...) ignores metro and term, and substitutes the STANDARD figure for an unlisted package with a note naming the substitution; egress(...) matches provider + path, ignoring region and term. The emitted notes identify the tier or substitution; the data vintage is available via asOf() (the engines surface it in their reports' "as of" line).

The bundled data set is loaded once from /json/ratecard_reference_2026_06.json and cached.

    • connection

      public Optional<PriceQuote> connection(ConnectionType type, int bandwidthMbps, MetroCode metro, Term term)
      Description copied from interface: RateCard
      Resolves the price of a single Fabric connection / virtual connection.

      Implementation contract. The matching strategy is implementation-specific, and a card whose data lacks an axis (metro, term, type) still returns its best figure — or empty — rather than failing; callers must not assume every card is sensitive to every parameter. Of the bundled cards: CustomRateCard resolves the most specific declared entry (exact metro+term down to metro/term-agnostic, then a declared default); EquinixRateCard matches bandwidth and type against the live catalogue, honours a requested metro strictly (a wrong-metro row is never returned), and prefers a term-matched row — a different-term row is only ever returned with a note naming the substitution; ReferenceRateCard matches on bandwidth alone (smallest tabulated tier at or above the request, linearly extrapolated with an EXTRAPOLATED note above the top tier) and ignores type, metro, and term entirely.

      Specified by:
      connection in interface RateCard
      Parameters:
      type - the connection type (e.g. EVPL_VC); may be null for any type
      bandwidthMbps - the provisioned bandwidth in Mbps
      metro - the metro the connection originates in (may be null if metro-agnostic)
      term - the commitment term (may be null if term-agnostic)
      Returns:
      the resolved quote, or Optional.empty() if this card cannot price the connection

    • cloudRouter

      public Optional<PriceQuote> cloudRouter(String packageCode, MetroCode metro, Term term)
      Description copied from interface: RateCard
      Resolves the price of a single Fabric Cloud Router instance.

      Implementation contract. As with RateCard.connection(ConnectionType, int, MetroCode, Term), matching is implementation-specific and cards without a metro/term axis return their best figure regardless. Of the bundled cards: CustomRateCard resolves the most specific declared (packageCode, metro, term) entry; EquinixRateCard matches the package code and metro structurally against the row's own descriptor (exact package equality, the row's own metro code) and prefers a term-matched row, labelling any term substitution; ReferenceRateCard ignores metro and term, and substitutes its STANDARD figure for an unlisted package with a note naming the substitution.

      Specified by:
      cloudRouter in interface RateCard
      Parameters:
      packageCode - the router package / tier code (e.g. "STANDARD"); may be null for any
      metro - the metro the router is deployed in (may be null if metro-agnostic)
      term - the commitment term (may be null if term-agnostic)
      Returns:
      the resolved quote, or Optional.empty() if this card cannot price the router

    • egress

      public Optional<EgressRate> egress(CloudProviderType provider, String region, EgressPath path, Term term)
      Description copied from interface: RateCard
      Resolves the per-GB data-egress rate for a cloud provider over a given path.

      Equinix does not sell cloud egress, so EquinixRateCard returns Optional.empty() here (the default); egress rates come from a CustomRateCard (your figures), a ReferenceRateCard (bundled indicative figures), or a provider-pricing-API card. The default returns empty so cards that do not model egress need not override it. Cards whose data has no region or term axis ignore those parameters — the custom and reference cards match on provider + path alone; only the provider-API adapters are region-sensitive.

      Specified by:
      egress in interface RateCard
      Parameters:
      provider - the cloud provider the data is leaving
      region - the provider region (may be null for a provider-wide rate)
      path - internet vs. private interconnect
      term - the commitment term (may be null; ignored by term-agnostic cards)
      Returns:
      the resolved egress rate, or Optional.empty() if this card cannot price it

    • onPrem

      public Optional<BigDecimal> onPrem(String key)
      An indicative on-premises cost midpoint by key. The bundled keys are:
      • "transitPerMbpsMonth" — carrier IP transit, per Mbps per month;
      • "crossConnectMonthly" — a carrier-hotel cross-connect, per month;
      • "hardwareMonthly" — amortized network hardware, per month;
      • "powerPerKwMonth" — power/space, per kW per month.
      These feed the TCO model's on-prem archetype and are individually overridable via the TcoCalculator.Builder.onPrem* methods.
      Parameters:
      key - one of the keys above
      Returns:
      the midpoint in the reference currency, or empty for an unknown key or an entry missing from the bundle

    • cspInterconnectPortMonthly

      public Optional<BigDecimal> cspInterconnectPortMonthly(CloudProviderType provider, int bandwidthMbps)
      The indicative monthly fee for a cloud provider's interconnect port/circuit (AWS Direct Connect / Azure ExpressRoute / GCP Interconnect) at or above the requested bandwidth. A request above the largest tabulated tier is never silently floored back to that tier's flat price (which would price a 100G requirement as a single 10G circuit) — it is extrapolated linearly from the top tier's per-Mbps rate, exactly as connection(...) does; use cspInterconnectPortMonthlyQuote(CloudProviderType, int) to see the extrapolation tag.
      Parameters:
      provider - the cloud provider
      bandwidthMbps - the desired bandwidth
      Returns:
      the reference monthly port fee (extrapolated above the top tabulated tier), or empty if none is tabulated
